identity.description:
Give each D4c experiment a method, a budget and a decision rule

This PR changes the D4c entry of `TICKETS.md`. It changes no code.

## Why

The D4c entry gave one line for each of six experiments, with no method and no decision rule. D4b and D8 showed what that costs: a paid run that could not be stopped and continued, an estimate that the first two cases broke, and a decision rule that could not fail. The principal also asked for wider questions.

## What changes

**Rules for every experiment.** A paid probe of two cases before a full run. A test that the decision rule can give each of its results. One paid run at a time. Records under the crew record root. No experiment has a budget: a run takes the plan windows that it needs, and each note reports its spend.

**Shared parts.** One reference run of the full pipeline with stored records (S1), a replay tool that verifies stored candidates again (S2), size groups of the cases (S3), and an eval option for the model and the effort of the reviewers (S4).

**The experiments:**

- **E1**: the model and the effort of every reviewer. Arms: Opus low (today), Opus medium, Sonnet medium, Sonnet high, on all 28 cases. One run of an arm measures all seven reviewers.
- **E2**: the specialist set against one Opus reviewer at medium, one at high, and one Terra reviewer at high effort. It reports by PR size and looks for the size where the specialists become better. It uses all 28 cases, with a second table by case source.
- **E3**: the model and the effort of the first verifier. Arms: Sonnet high (today), Sonnet medium, Opus low, Terra medium, on the same stored candidates. Opus medium runs only if Opus low passes. The note reports truth and severity apart.
- **E3b**: where the severity label comes from. One verifier call for truth and severity, as today, against a verifier for truth and a separate severity step, for each finding or for each PR.
- **E4, E5, E6**: the score scale, the cap, and a prompt injection. Each has a method and a rule.
- **E7**: the five follow-ups that name D4c. The S1 records answer two of them with no model call, among them the passes of diff-bugs and security.

**Second-family models.** Each Codex arm states its reasoning effort. This round uses Terra; the Sol arms are for a later round.

## What a reviewer must check

- **E1 and the noise between runs.** Two arms of E1 are two runs, so they are not paired. The entry requires the note to report the noise of one pass and to claim no smaller difference.
- **E3b and the goldens.** The severity labels of the goldens came from the labeler, which is Opus with a Sol judge. A severity step on Opus can agree with those labels for that reason. The note must state this limit.
- **The numbers in the rules** (two times the cost, 0.05, 90% intervals) follow the D8 rule.

## Verification

`npm test` (1503 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

below_floor.span_text: - Cases: all 28. The S1 records are the first arm. The D8 measurement records hold two more passes of history and of tests at Opus 5.5 low on the same cases; use them as more samples of the first arm for those two reviewers. - Passes: run E7 first. Each arm uses the pass defaults that E7 leaves, so a reviewer that E7 moves to one pass runs one pass in every arm. - Two stages. Stage 1 runs the reviewers of each new arm with no verifier, and matches the raw candidates to the goldens. A golden that an arm did not raise cannot be posted by it, so stage 1 is sufficient to reject a setting that raises fewer posted-label goldens than the current one, less the noise of one pass, for no lower cost. Stage 2 sends to the verifier, through S2, only the candidates of the reviewer and arm pairs that stage 1 did not reject.
